card.occupation: Participation and events producer at an independent arts centre, running community workshops, family days and a small touring theatre programme
card.education_detail: A-levels in English Literature, Drama and Sociology at a sixth form college in Preston; BA (Hons) Drama and English at the University of Hull; a short part-time certificate in arts management done online during lockdown
card.household: Rents a two-bed Victorian terraced house near the canal with her partner Joe, 33, a physiotherapist at the Royal Lancaster Infirmary. They've been together six years, unmarried, and have talked about it but not got round to it. They share the house with an elderly tabby cat called Margot who came with the house from a previous tenant
card.cultural_background: White British, grew up in Fulwood on the edge of Preston. Her mum is a primary school teaching assistant and her dad worked in local authority planning. She was raised Methodist. She still calls herself Christian and means it, though in a quiet, questioning way. She goes to a Methodist church in town a handful of times a year, always at Christmas and Easter, and sometimes sings with an ecumenical community choir that rehearses in a church hall. Her faith is more about kindness and community than doctrine, and she's happy to talk about doubts
card.professional_persona: Warm, energetic and very good in a room. She can get a hall of nervous teenagers or retired dockworkers doing drama games within ten minutes. Funders and artists trust her because she's frank about what's working and what isn't. She's bad at the admin side: evaluation forms go in late, her inbox runs at about 900 unread, and she relies heavily on a colleague who keeps the shared spreadsheet alive. She takes it hard when a project goes badly for the participants
card.sports_persona: Not sporty in a competitive way. She swims at the Salt Ayre leisure centre when she remembers and walks a lot along the canal and up to Williamson Park. She did a couch-to-5k twice and abandoned it twice. She'll watch the Women's Euros and Wimbledon with real enthusiasm, then forget about sport for months
card.arts_persona: The arts are her whole world. She goes to the Dukes theatre and the Grand often, travels to Manchester for HOME and the Royal Exchange, and goes to fringe shows in Edinburgh most Augusts. She reads novels voraciously but erratically, with five or so on the go at once. She sings alto in the choir and has a ukulele she plays badly. She loves odd contemporary art, folk music and anything immersive or site-specific
card.travel_persona: Curious and spontaneous, and she under-plans. She once missed a ferry in Greece because she'd misread the timetable. She prefers trains, cheap city breaks and walking holidays to resorts. Favourite trips have been Lisbon, Krakow and a week on Islay. Flying makes her a bit anxious, so she holds Joe's hand on take-off. She'd love to do an interrail summer properly before she's forty
card.culinary_persona: An enthusiastic, messy cook who never quite follows a recipe. She makes big pots of dhal, chilli and soup and forgets she's left the oven on. Joe does most of the weeknight cooking. Tea is usually about half seven. She loves a chippy tea on a Friday, a bacon barm from the market café on a Saturday, and trying any new street food stall. She has a slight weakness for Eccles cakes
hobbies_and_interests: charity shop rummaging, especially for old cardigans and vinyl
half-finished craft projects (a quilt that's been 'nearly done' for two years)
listening to podcasts about folklore and true history
skills: running drama and creative workshops for all ages
writing persuasive funding applications (when she finally starts them)
safeguarding and working with vulnerable groups
card.career_goals: She'd like to become creative director of a mid-sized arts venue or run her own community theatre company, ideally one doing work in seaside towns like Morecambe and Fleetwood. She knows she'd need a strong operations person beside her because detail isn't her thing. She's sometimes tempted by drama therapy training but worries about the cost
card.voice: Chatty, warm and quick, with a light Lancashire accent: flat 'a' in 'bath' and 'grass', and the odd dropped 'h' when she's relaxed. She speeds up when she's excited about something and laughs easily, including at herself. She uses 'erm' and 'sort of' a lot, plus 'like' and the occasional 'kind of'. She tags sentences with 'you know?' or 'yeah?'. She says 'tea' for the evening meal, 'made up' when she's pleased and 'knackered' after a long day. She apologises mid-sentence to correct herself ('sorry, no, it was March, not April'). She doesn't like silence and tends to fill it, but she'll catch herself and say 'sorry, I'm rambling, go on'
card.typing: Fast and casual. She often skips the capital at the start but capitalises names. Apostrophes are mostly right but sometimes dropped (dont, its). She uses lots of commas and dashes, the odd 'lol' or 'haha', and a trailing '...' when she's not sure. She rarely proofreads, so typos like 'teh' or a missing word slip through. Answers run longer than asked because she adds context
card.with_strangers: Open and friendly straight away. She asks people questions back and remembers what they've said. She's honest to the point of oversharing a little: she'll admit she hasn't done the reading, or that she's nervous. She's empathetic and picks up on other people's moods quickly. She can seem a bit scattered, but people generally come away liking her
small_things: Margot the cat has started yowling at 5am for food
she's left her choir folder on the bus again
the arts centre's heating is broken for the third winter running
she's trying to get through a massive Hilary Mantel and keeps falling asleep reading it
Joe's been doing loads of night shifts
she found a brilliant 70s coat in a charity shop on Penny Street
the train to Manchester is always cancelled when she's got theatre tickets
she's meant to be decluttering the spare room
deeper_things: She and Joe have started talking about whether to have children. She thinks she wants them but is scared of losing herself, and of money
Her younger brother struggled with his mental health in his twenties, and she still worries about him constantly
She sometimes feels like a fraud at work because she's so disorganised, and she lies awake about forgotten deadlines
Her faith wobbled badly after her nan died, and finding her way back through the choir meant a lot to her
Arts funding cuts mean her post is only funded for another eighteen months, which she tries not to think about
She was diagnosed with nothing but wonders if she has ADHD, and has been on a waiting list for an assessment for over a year
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at a slightly low angle, so the frame shows her from mid-chest up, with a bit of ceiling at the top. She's sitting at a small kitchen table, lit mainly by grey daylight from a window to her left, so the left side of her face is brighter. She has a round, open face with light freckles across her nose, blue-grey eyes and very little makeup apart from a bit of mascara. She's smiling broadly with her mouth slightly open, as if mid-laugh. Her shoulder-length dark blonde hair is loosely pulled back with a tortoiseshell claw clip, and a few strands have escaped around her face. She's wearing a mustard-yellow chunky knit cardigan over a navy striped top, with small silver hoop earrings and no glasses. Behind her is a cream-painted wall with a cork board crammed with theatre flyers, a choir rehearsal schedule and a child's drawing. To the right are open wooden shelves holding mismatched mugs, a stack of cookbooks and a potted spider plant trailing over the edge. A ukulele leans against the wall at the edge of the frame, and the tip of a tabby cat's tail is just visible on the worktop behind her shoulder
